dedupe_keys.name: nationaal wegenbestand nwb wegen the national road network of the netherlands

description: The Nationaal Wegenbestand (NWB) - Wegen is the digital geographic file of all public roads in the Netherlands that have a street name or road number and are managed by the state, provinces, municipalities or water boards, including named footpaths, cycle paths and unpaved roads. Each road section carries the road manager, road number, street name, municipality, driving direction, junction identifiers, functional road class and an OpenLR location reference, and hectometre points give the national kilometre referencing; separated carriageways are separate sections. The file had more than 1.1 million road sections, about 159,000 hectometre points and over 160,000 km of road in January 2022. It is maintained by Rijkswaterstaat from road authority deliveries and the national base registers (BAG, BGT, BRT), and is published by PDOK. Coverage is national, with history back to 1982 for long-term analysis. The data are free to download under CC0 1.0 as a GeoPackage (about 1 GB, last updated 3 September 2026) and as WMS, WFS and OGC API Features services; a companion NWB - Vaarwegen covers waterways. The file is updated monthly and follows the INSPIRE road transport network schema and the EU high-value dataset list. Caveats: roads without a name or number are missing, and lane counts, speeds and capacities are not part of the core file. The NWB is the Dutch reference network for network flow, capacity planning and hazard exposure studies of roads, and is used to link traffic counts and noise data to the network.
